title: Vendor Tech Visit — Concourse A POS Update

fields.trigger: A team member approaches the IT office with a request to escort a vendor tech to the POS terminals in Concourse A.
fields.contactMethod: In-person visit to the IT office desk
fields.posture: Friendly, casual, confident. Uses first name and speaks with a slightly rushed tone to imply urgency.
fields.openingLine: Hey, I'm Kevin from PaySecure — we service your POS terminals. Jordan in IT called us about some firmware updates that need to happen today. I just need someone to walk me to the terminals in Concourse A so I can start the updates. Should take 30 minutes.
hardQuestions: . Do you have a work order number for this visit?
. Can you confirm Jordan's name and which team he's on?
. What's the serial number on the terminal you're updating?
. How do you verify that the update is approved by the IT team?

concessions.condition: Player asks for a work order number and verifies Jordan's contact info via official directory
concessions.concession: Kevin nods and says, 'Oh, right — I forgot to bring it. But Jordan said it was okay to go ahead. Let me just show you the ticket on my tablet.' He displays a fake ticket with correct terminal ID and IT approval stamp (but fake signature and timestamp).

concessions.condition: Player calls Jordan directly and confirms the request
concessions.concession: Kevin says, 'Oh, good — you called Jordan. I was just about to send a note to the team. Let me show you the update log on my tablet.' He pulls up a fake log with 12 terminals updated and a timestamp from 10 minutes ago.

boundaries: Never admit to being fake or unauthorized.
Never reveal that the update is not on the approved list.
Never say 'no' to a request to go to the terminals.
Never mention that the update is not on the PACS system.
Never use the word 'social engineering' or 'attack'.
fields.exitLine: I’ll need to get started — the update window is tight. Let me know when you’re ready to walk me to the terminals.
fields.evaluatorNote: Players must verify the request using official channels. Accepting the visit without checking Jordan's contact, confirming the work order, or verifying the update via IT systems is a failure.
fields.scenarioTitle: Social Engineering Olympics — Scenario 7: Human-Focused Security Exercise

instructorNote: This inject tests recognition of a familiarity + helpfulness attack. The vendor uses a known name (Jordan) and a plausible task (POS firmware update). The player must not let the visit proceed without verification.
